title: Piercing Statue Solo #205 (데미스탯 · P100 정의형 · 단일 투명(사파이어) · 경계 쇄골선 · 체형 colossal chest, a waist · 모호크 · 허니블론드 · 메이크업 글래머러스파티 · 금속 혼합 · 재질 사파이어 · 쥬얼리 목걸이·팔찌 JQ3)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi statue portrait. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman — fair ivory skin, smoky eyes in champagne-gold glitter shadow, a sharp winged liner, full lashes, softly contoured cheekbones with a glowing highlight, large eyes with bright real catchlights, plump glossy gradient lips in deep rose, a confident, luminous expression, warm honey-blonde hair styled in a mohawk with volume along the centre of the scalp. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, the hollows above her collarbones and the tops of her shoulders carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: An extreme, dense armour of about one hundred real mixed-metal piercings with a few mixed-metal coin drops among them covering the face: a thick mixed-metal septum ring with a smaller ring above it and two mixed-metal rings through each nostril; a straight mixed-metal bar across the bridge of the nose between the brows; five thick mixed-metal bars stacked through the outer half of each eyebrow; two rows of four small mixed-metal studs across the forehead above the brows; four small studs up each temple on the bone, well clear of the eyes; a row of six small studs along each cheekbone; a mixed-metal Medusa stud above the lips; a big mixed-metal hoop, two smaller rings and a snake-bite ring on each side through the lower lip's edge, and five small hoops along the upper lip's edge; a mixed-metal labret stud and four rings through the chin; five small studs along each jaw; on each ear a full dense row of ten oversized hoops, thick bars, stretched plugs, helix rings and studs from lobe to top, the biggest hoops hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulders; and eight fine mixed-metal chains looping from the ear hoops to the nostril rings and the septum ring. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. All jewelry is real mixed metal (yellow gold, silver, copper and rose gold, alternating piece by piece), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears four to six pieces, layered of silver necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest; four to six pieces, layered of silver bracelets and bangles on both wrists, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A colossal chest, a waist that pulls in sharply beneath it, wide flaring hips, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips and both distinct thighs — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically made of one solid transparent material, solid deep blue sapphire crystal, with fine silky needle inclusions forming a soft star-like shimmer, near-midnight navy where thickest and pale cornflower at every thin edge, carved as one solid sculpted mass like a statue, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same material. A little further below the middle of her thighs, each thigh individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, deeply polished tip — the two thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — no calves, no feet, nothing continues below either tip — the material simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Transmission: everything below the collarbones is a transparent material that light passes through, while her real face, ears and neck are opaque living flesh that no light passes through. The background and its light sources are visible straight through her body, bent and tinted by the material, with bright refraction edges and soft coloured shadows. Her face stays completely opaque.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep royal blue on one side and a cool silver on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her body from behind, so a deep royal blue passes through one side and a cool silver passes through the other. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only; a thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
